title: Person, Action, Object
tagline: A film director with a cast of a hundred and a million possible scenes. Six digits become one picture.
card: The champion's number system: a person, an action and an object, so that six digits fit in one picture.
goal: you will learn how PAO packs six digits into one scene, build your own list of a hundred people with their actions and objects, and encode and decode six-digit numbers.

left_off.q: In the Dominic System, how do you hold four digits?
left_off.a: The person of the first pair doing the action of the second pair.

left_off.q: What letter is 7 in the Dominic System? And 0?
Why are people stronger pictures than plain words?
left_off.a: A person has a face, a voice, a way of moving and something they do, so there is more to see and hold.

text: Imagine you are the assistant director on a film set, and the director has a strange rule. Every scene must contain exactly three things: a person, something that person does, and something they do it with. A woman paints a wall with a feather. A knight kisses a goat with a trumpet. A soldier cooks a pie in a bathtub.
The director shouts a number at the start of each scene, and your job is to remember all the scenes in order. The first number is 341526. Without thinking, the cast takes its places.

check.q: What three things must every scene contain?
check.a: A person, an action, and an object.

parts.talk: Invent a scene with a person, an action and an object that has nothing to do with each other. Describe it.

text: The reason the film works is that a scene has just three ingredients, but there are so many possible combinations. If there are a hundred people on the cast list, a hundred actions and a hundred objects, then the director can make a million different scenes, and no two are alike.

In this story every scene corresponds to six digits. The first two digits choose the person, the next two choose the action, and the last two choose the object. 34 is Charles Darwin. 15 is a certain action, 26 is a certain object. And so the scene for 341526 is Darwin, doing the action that belongs to 15, with the object that belongs to 26.

check.q: How many different scenes can the cast of a hundred people, a hundred actions and a hundred objects make?

parts.talk: Why would a million possible scenes be useful to a memory athlete?

text: That is the idea of the PAO system: Person, Action, Object. It grew out of the Dominic System of the last lesson, which used person and action only, and it is used by many memory champions in competitions. One scene holds six digits, so a twelve-digit number needs just two pictures.

You will need to build the cast list yourself: a hundred people, each with one action and one object. It takes some work. But once it is built, you have a piece of equipment you can use all your life.

check.q: How is PAO related to the Dominic System?
check.a: Dominic uses a person and an action; PAO adds a third element, the object, so each picture holds six digits.

parts.talk: How long do you think it would take to build a list of a hundred people, actions and objects? What would help?

words.m: a thing you can see or touch. The object is a guitar.
a mixture of things put together. A million combinations.
the people in a film or play.
to put pieces together. Assemble the scene from three pieces.
using little time or effort for the result. PAO is efficient: six digits in one picture.
made to suit one person. Your own list is personalised.

source: PAO is a standard technique in memory sport. Our own explanation.

method.x: Every two-digit pair, 00 to 99, has three entries: a person, an action and an object. You learn them once. Then any six digits become one scene.

items.h: Split the number into pairs of digits.
Take the PERSON of the first pair.
Take the ACTION of the second pair.
items.x: 15 → the action of Albert Einstein: writing on a blackboard.

items.h: Take the OBJECT of the third pair.
items.x: 26 → the object of Bruce Springsteen: a guitar.
Darwin is writing on a blackboard, with a guitar for a piece of chalk.

method.title: A full PAO scene
lines: Action: writing on a blackboard (Einstein's action).
method.pic: Charles Darwin is writing on a blackboard with a guitar instead of a piece of chalk, and the strings sing as they scratch.

method.x: A model list to start from
Use these to begin, then replace them with people and things that are vivid for you.

items: Person: use the Dominic initials (digits to letters). Choose people who are easy to see: film stars, sports people, family, friends.
Action: choose the thing they are best known for. Make it big and physical.
Object: choose something you can see them holding. Try not to use the same object twice.
Keep entries different. If two people use a guitar, one of them will leak into the other.
Start with a few. Build ten pairs a day and test yourself.

method.x:
P from the first pair.
A from the second.
O from the third.
six digits, one scene.
Decoding works the other way. You see Darwin writing on a blackboard with a guitar: Darwin is 34, the action is Einstein's (15), the object is Springsteen's (26). So 341526.
Odd lengths. If the number does not divide by six, finish with a smaller scene: two digits = a person, four digits = person + action.
Say aloud the PAO scene for 101323 using the model list, and explain which pair gave each part.

items.s: P stands for person, A for action and O for ___.
With a hundred people, a hundred actions and a hundred objects you can make one ___ different scenes.

try.title: Assemble 241813
try.prompt: Use the model list. 24 gives the person, 18 gives the action, 13 gives the object. Write the scene.
try.model: Person: Bob Dylan (24). Action of 18: Hitchcock's action, filming. Object of 13: Al Capone's briefcase. Scene: Bob Dylan is filming a shower scene with a briefcase, and every time he presses the camera a harmonica note comes out.

try.title: Assemble 162734
try.prompt: 16 for the person, 27 for the action, 34 for the object. Write the scene.
try.model: Person: Arnold Schwarzenegger (16). Action of 27: typing (Bill Gates). Object of 34: a finch. Arnold is typing furiously on a keyboard with a tiny finch, which pecks the keys and sings.

try.title: Decode a scene
try.prompt: A scene: Al Oerter is lecturing with a saxophone. Which six digits does it hold? (Use the model list.)
try.model: Al Oerter = 10. Lecturing is Al Gore's action = 17. A saxophone is Bill Clinton's object = 23. So the number is 101723.

try.title: Make your own entry
try.prompt: Pick a pair that is not in the model list (for example 40, 41 or 42). Work out the initials, find a person, an action and an object.
try.model: There is no single answer. Check that the initials are right for the two digits, that the person is vivid and that the action and object are different from the ones above.
checks: The initials match the two digits.
The action is something I can see.
The object is different from the others.

opts: Person of 10, action of 13, object of 23
Person of 23, action of 10, object of 13
try.why: First pair gives the person, second the action, third the object. 10 = Al Oerter, action of 13 = counting money, object of 23 = a saxophone.

try.title: Tell the scene
try.prompt: Say aloud the scene for 101323, then the scene for 341526, and say which digits each part stands for.

cards: Person, Action, Object: one scene holds six digits.
Albert Einstein, writing on a blackboard, with chalk.
Find the person's pair, the action's pair and the object's pair, in that order.
Finish with a smaller scene: person for two digits, person + action for four.

quiz.q: In PAO, what does the second pair of digits give you?
quiz.why: Person, action, object: first, second, third.

quiz.q: Why is PAO more efficient than the Dominic System?
opts: It holds six digits in one scene instead of four
quiz.why: Dominic holds four digits in a scene; PAO holds six.

quiz.q: What is the best way to build your PAO list?
opts: Copy a ready-made one and never change it
Build ten pairs a day with people and things vivid to you
Learn all 300 entries in one evening
quiz.why: Your own list is stronger, and slow steady building is more reliable.

quiz.q: Why should you avoid using the same object for two people?
quiz.why: Two entries that share an object leak into each other and you cannot tell which is which.

challenge.title: Memory challenge: ten objects
challenge.intro: These are the objects of the pairs 10, 13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 23, 24, 26 and 27 in the model list. Learn them in order and say the pair as you place each one in your palace.
challenge.study: One object at each place of your palace, doing something to the place.
